prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your exact location, budget, system type, timeline and service expectations. I can help you find the best option for your situation. To do that I’ll need your ZIP code (or neighborhood) and any preferences (brands, budget, timeline).

Meanwhile, here’s a short checklist and what to ask so you get a high-quality replacement:

What to require from every contractor
- Proof of license and insurance (ask for license number).  
- NATE-certified technicians or equivalent credentials.  
- A Manual J load calculation (not just “match the old unit”) to size the system properly.  
- A written, line-item estimate including equipment model numbers, SEER rating, labor, permits, disposal, tax and warranty details.  
- Manufacturer and workmanship warranties in writing (ask how long each lasts and who services warranty work).  
- Local references or recent online reviews (Google, Yelp, BBB).  
- Permit and inspection handling included in the price.

Questions to ask during the estimate
- Why did you recommend this tonnage and SEER? Can I see the Manual J?  
- Which brands/models do you install and are you a certified dealer for them?  
- What is included in the install (new thermostat, duct modifications, refrigerant, condensate lines, permitting)?  
- What’s the timeline for the job? Who will be on site?  
- Do you offer financing, maintenance plans, or annual tune-ups?  
- How do you handle warranty/after-hours service calls?

How to choose
- Get at least 3 written bids and compare scope, not just price.  
- Prefer contractors who perform a Manual J and show you the calculations.  
- Choose one with strong local reviews and documented warranty handling.  
- Avoid very low bids that cut scope or use vague descriptions.

Other tips
- Consider higher SEER for long-term savings if your ductwork and budget allow.  
- Check for utility rebates and federal tax credits for high-efficiency systems.  
- Keep documentation and the receipts — important for warranty and resale.

If you want, give me your ZIP code (and whether this is a single-family home, townhouse, or condo, plus any brand preferences or budget range) and I’ll pull together 3–5 well-reviewed local HVAC companies and highlight their strengths for an AC replacement.
